correctness.rationale: Circulant Fourier diagonalization gives the exact eigenvalues. The Poisson-summation positive theta term is bounded below by sqrt(pi/t)exp(-pi^2/(4t)), while all omitted tails are bounded by 2exp(-tn^2/4)/(1-exp(-tn)). For t>=(pi+epsilon)/n the ratio is uniformly exponentially small through t=1, and diagonal dominance covers all t>=1. For t=c/n with c<pi, an even-N near-Nyquist tail has positive limiting factor (1-exp(-c))/(1+exp(-c)), and an odd-N sine-weighted near-Nyquist tail has positive limiting factor (1-exp(-c))/(2(1+exp(-c))^2). These exponentially dominate the positive theta term and yield negative eigenvalues in all residue classes. The squeezed limit follows. The packaged checker passed high-precision representative computations; it is not substituted for the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The sharpened all-cycle leading constant n*tau_n -> pi for the last negative-eigenvalue scale was not implied by the inspected global all-bandwidth geometric theorems, the 2016 finite random-sample open questions, or the 2023 no-fixed-scale circle theorem. Its key new implication is uniform positivity at all t>(pi+eps)/n combined with a negative near-Nyquist witness at t=(pi-eps)/n for every parity class. Bounded literature and published-record searches did not locate an equivalent or stronger statement; the 1995 historical circle covariance article remains a named access risk.

value.rationale: Sharp limiting value pi for the deterministic last-indefiniteness scale of geodesic Gaussian kernel matrices on every uniform n-point circle answers the finite-dataset bandwidth admissibility question motivated in the 2016 literature. The value comes from a nontrivial asymptotic competition of theta decay and antipodal truncation, with a different polynomial prefactor in odd cycles. In unit circle normalization it gives the practically interpretable leading scale lambda~n/(4pi), quantifying the continuum no-go result rather than merely restating it.
